name: @material-tax-reporting/local-ollama
description: Local-only Ollama model store, pull queue, chat, and allowlisted harness orchestration.
//: The '.' entry is the TypeScript source, and it stays that way because every
consumer of this package is a bundler. An exhaustive sweep for this package's
name finds exactly two importers. The desktop main process reaches it only
through the esbuild bundle that apps/desktop/scripts/build.mjs writes and that
workspace's 'main' field points at, so Node never loads the requiring file
itself. The documentation site additionally rewrites the specifier to an
absolute source path in apps/site/vite.pages.config.ts and in
apps/site/src/checks/render-smoke.config.ts, so this map is not consulted there
at all. This package's own tests import relative paths under
--experimental-strip-types and never use the package name.
The trap, recorded so nobody has to rediscover it: the first file Node
executes directly that imports this package by name dies on that import with
ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION naming src/index.ts. Node cannot load a '.ts' file;
it strips types only when asked, and not by default until 22.18.0, which is
newer than the 22.14.0 toolchain this repository pins. Reproduced against this
package on 2026-08-15 by importing src/index.ts under
'node --no-experimental-strip-types', which reproduces the pinned runtime's
default behaviour on a newer local Node.
The remedy then is the shape packages/surface-kernel already uses: a 'node'
condition beside this one resolving to a dist/index.js transpiled by esbuild -
never by tsc, which also type-checks and so could withhold a release - with
@material-tax-reporting/surface-kernel left external, because src/catalog.ts and
src/controller.ts import its values and not only its types, and bundling a
second copy into a consumer that already carries one would give that consumer
two module instances. The artifact has to exist before anything resolves the
condition, so the same change must also add this package to the 'prebuild'
script of every workspace that bundles it, exactly as apps/desktop already does
for the surface kernel. Whether esbuild's Node platform selects the 'node'
condition was not measured when this note was written, so treat that hook as
required rather than optional: if it does select it, adding the condition alone
would break the desktop build, which is on the release path.
There is deliberately no 'build' script. TypeScript is declared by no manifest
in this repository and no tsc binary is installed, so the 'tsc -p tsconfig.json'
script that used to sit here had never run and emitted nothing. tsconfig.json is
kept for editors and for a hand-run 'tsc --noEmit' check.
